paragraphs.body: This is separate from everything else in D.A. G.O.A.T. Turning it on changes nothing about your Contribute settings, and leaving it off limits no other part of the app.

paragraphs.heading: What you are switching on
paragraphs.body: Your computer fetches web pages on behalf of other people and sends the results back. Those requests leave your home internet connection.

paragraphs.heading: Websites see your home address, not ours
paragraphs.body: Every site contacted this way records your household's IP address as the source of the request. Nothing points it at us instead of you.

paragraphs.heading: Your internet provider may cancel your account
paragraphs.body: Most residential provider agreements forbid relaying other people's traffic. Enforcement is usually suspension or cancellation, with no appeal.

paragraphs.heading: Your household may be locked out of ordinary websites
paragraphs.body: Addresses seen relaying traffic get added to proxy-detection lists. The result is repeated CAPTCHAs, streaming services refusing to play, and bank or shopping sites blocking sign-in, on every device in your home, including phones and consoles that never ran this app. That can outlast uninstalling.

paragraphs.heading: Police may contact the subscriber at this address
paragraphs.body: An IP address is the only identifier a site keeps. If a request made through your connection is investigated, it is traced to whoever pays for the line at this address.

paragraphs.heading: What is recorded
paragraphs.body: Only the allowlist entry contacted, the address it resolved to, and byte counts. No page contents, no paths, and no search terms are stored anywhere.

paragraphs.heading: The destination allowlist is fixed and inspectable
paragraphs.body: Requests can only reach the destinations listed on this screen. Everything else is refused before a socket opens, including addresses inside your own home network. The fingerprint of that list is part of what you sign.

paragraphs.heading: Caps and hours are held by the background process
paragraphs.body: Your daily limit, speed limit, and time window are enforced by the background process, not by this window. Closing D.A. G.O.A.T. does not lift them.

paragraphs.heading: Off until you sign, one click to stop
paragraphs.body: This stays off until you sign the record below. Switching it off halts traffic within five seconds.

paragraphs.heading: You re-confirm every 90 days
paragraphs.body: The signed record expires after 90 days, and immediately whenever this text or the allowlist changes. Traffic stops until you read the new text and sign again.
No GOAT is created by this. Nothing here is a promise of payment, and testnet GOAT has no monetary value.
